priorFindingsResolved.evidence: cart_v2.is_enabled() is an opt-in again: it returns False unless WIX_CART_V2_ENABLED is truthy, with WIX_CART_V2_DISABLED retained as an override on top of the opt-in rather than as a replacement. Both keys are absent from config/lambda-env-manifest.json (grep -o 'WIX_CART_V2[A-Z_]*' returns nothing), so the live answer is False on every function. Still one shared function, so the cart route and the checkout handler cannot disagree. Pinned by test_cart_v2_is_off_when_nothing_is_configured, test_the_opt_in_key_turns_it_on, test_a_non_truthy_opt_in_value_leaves_it_off, test_the_disable_key_overrides_a_deployed_opt_in, and two route-level tests whose _wix_request stub fails the test if ever reached.

_v2_snapshot resolves LOAD_OWNED_ADDRESS and raises DeliveryDetailsRequired before cart_v2.CartV2 is constructed, so no Wix write can precede the address check. test_without_an_owned_address_the_handler_refuses_before_touching_wix asserts wix.calls == [], measuring the absent call rather than the 409, and test_an_empty_profile_address_is_not_coerced_into_a_default does the same for {}/None/''. The abandoned-cart-per-attempt leak is removed. The loader itself is still unwired, which is now recorded as an open feature gate in three places and is carried forward as finding WIX-V2-006.

CustomerCart gained resolve() (read-only, raises CartBusy on a locked row, authorize_resource enforced, expired row reads as absent) and ensure() returning (cart_id, created), with creation routed through the existing execute so the lock protocol, the duplicate-request fingerprint and the persistence stay in one place. _v2_snapshot calls customer_cart.CustomerCart(_keys_table(), adapter).ensure(identity, requested) and only calls _require_same_basket when the cart was reused. execute claims the row with a conditional put before calling Wix, so two concurrent first attempts cannot both create. CartBusy maps to 409 CART_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED, the vocabulary /wix-store/cart already uses. Pinned by test_ensure_creates_once_and_then_resolves_the_same_cart, test_a_repeated_checkout_reuses_the_saved_cart_instead_of_minting_another (counts POST /ecom/v2/carts across two attempts), test_resolve_refuses_a_cart_whose_last_wix_outcome_is_unknown and test_resolve_will_not_hand_one_customers_cart_to_another.

The stale configured:'V1' paragraph and its configured:'V2' replacement are now one paragraph reading V1, with the inversion recorded as a reverted revision and its reasoning kept. configured is 'V1', drift moved to 'lag-allowed-with-reason' with upgradeBlockedReason and lagExpiresOn:'2026-12-31'. Not a quiet gate relaxation: WIX_ECOM_CART is a new row split from the old WIX_ECOM entry, which was configured:'V1' against a verifiedLatest of V1 and passed must-be-latest trivially; with verifiedLatest now 'V2' the strict setting would fail on code that is in fact migrated, and lag-allowed-with-reason is the schema's own mechanism for that. config/vendor-versions.json and docs/compatibility.md were brought back to V1 with it.

Recorded verification is still self-reported (6187 passed / 1 skipped, npm run typecheck exit 0, node scripts/check-versions.ts exit 0). This review was instructed not to re-run the suite, so none of it was independently reproduced. Carried forward as finding WIX-V2-009.

findings.problem: NON-BLOCKING. LOAD_OWNED_ADDRESS is still None at module scope and is assigned only in tests/test_checkout_cart_v2_authority.py, so an operator who sets WIX_CART_V2_ENABLED=true gets a checkout that answers 409 DELIVERY_DETAILS_REQUIRED on every request. There is no production impact today because the gate is off on all 65 functions, and the gap is honestly recorded in three places (the handler docstring, WIX_ECOM_CART.upgradeBlockedReason, and section 10 of docs/execution/wix-cart-v2-migration-20261001.md, which calls the address source an owner decision rather than inventing one). What is missing is a refusal: is_enabled() answers True on the environment variable alone, so the incoherent combination of an enabled gate and an unwired loader is discovered by customers rather than at initialisation. This repo already has the opposite pattern -- meta_version._resolve raises MetaVersionError at import when META_API_VERSION and META_GRAPH_BASE disagree, deliberately declining to pick a winner.
findings.fix: Make the incoherent combination fail at configuration time rather than per request: have is_enabled() (or checkout module init) refuse when the gate is on and no address loader is wired, following meta_version._resolve's raise-at-import pattern. Wire LOAD_OWNED_ADDRESS to the authenticated customer's stored profile address -- never the request body, since the address sets the India place of supply -- as a precondition of enabling the gate.

findings.problem: NON-BLOCKING. The saved-cart comparison reads lineItems[].source.catalogReference and quantityInfo.requestedQuantity out of a live cart GET. cart_v2.calculate already relies on the same nesting, so no new unverified shape was introduced, but the consequence of a mismatch is new: calculate raises CartContractError('unsupported or unavailable catalog item') on an unexpected nesting, whereas _require_same_basket produces {('',''): n} on the saved side, mismatches unconditionally, and refuses every reused cart. Fail-closed and the correct direction, but it would present as 409 CART_NOT_PAYABLE to every returning customer with only the checkout_cart_basket_mismatch log event to explain it. The migration doc already names six V2 request shapes as convention-derived and unverified against a live call; the cart GET line-item nesting belongs on that same list.
findings.fix: Add the cart GET lineItems[].source.catalogReference and quantityInfo nesting to the one authorized live Calculate Cart verification that is already recorded as the deploy gate, so the reuse comparison is confirmed against a real response before the gate is opened.

findings.problem: NON-BLOCKING. A basket mismatch raises the generic cart_v2.CartContractError, so the customer-facing answer is 409 CART_NOT_PAYABLE / 'Please review your cart and try again' -- the same response given for blocking violations, unsupported catalog items, an empty cart and a line calculation disagreement. The distinguishing information exists only in the checkout_cart_basket_mismatch log line, so a client cannot tell the customer that their saved cart changed as opposed to that it cannot be priced, and the two need different actions from them.
findings.fix: Raise a distinct exception (for example cart_v2.CartBasketChanged) from _require_same_basket and map it to its own error code with the saved-versus-requested line counts, keeping CART_NOT_PAYABLE for genuine contract violations.

findings.where: amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/customer_cart.py:74-94 (ensure docstring and resolve expiry branch); commit 089ba325 message
findings.problem: NON-BLOCKING, two informational points. First: ensure()'s docstring states 'One purchase has one cart', which holds within CART_LIFETIME but not across it -- resolve() treats an expired row as absent, and execute('create') carries wixCartId forward only when the row is active, so a checkout after expiry creates a fresh Wix cart and leaves the previous one on the live site with nothing to complete or delete it. The expiry mechanism predates this commit and belongs to the /wix-store/cart route, so it is not a regression; what is new is the unqualified guarantee in a new docstring. Second: the recorded verification (6187 passed / 1 skipped, npm run typecheck exit 0, node scripts/check-versions.ts exit 0) is self-reported and was not reproduced, since this review was instructed not to re-run the suite.
findings.fix: Bound the docstring claim to the cart lifetime, or reconcile the expired wixCartId when a replacement cart is created. Let CI reproduce the test, typecheck and version-gate results on this tree; no coder action needed for that half.
